subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a vehicle model, deciding to keep it static and skip joints since static models can omit them entirely, with parts assigned without bone hierarchy.

Now I'm sketching the actual design: a six-wheel armored truck roughly 7m long, with a cab, cargo bed, roof turret, neon glow strips, headlights, and decal textures, built from boxes and extruded shapes with cylinder wheels rotated along the x-axis, pulling flat colors and panel/glow styling from the kit imports while working out axle placement along the z-axis.

Working out chassis and cab geometry...

Computing the windshield box placement and tilt angle so its top edge slants backward correctly, working out the rotation about X to orient the normal up-and-forward.

Next I'm positioning the glass glow color, then adding armor plates, side skirts, a front bull bar, and headlight bars positioned at the front face near z=3.3.

I'm placing a light strip on the hood's leading edge, then sizing a front bumper box with a hazard chevron decal texture on its forward face. For the cargo section, I'm building an armored container with paneling, topped by angled missile launcher pods near the rear.

I'm also planning a cab-roof turret with a ring base, twin barrels and sensor, plus container side panels with "NEO-ARES 2077" branding, vertical ribs, magenta neon strips, and cyan underglow beneath the chassis—alongside an antenna array, radar dish, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, mirrors, and headlights.

Now I'm working out wheel and chassis geometry carefully, adding rear tail lights, bumper, double rear doors with texture, tires with glowing hub rings and bolts, and fender boxes above the wheels—making sure the cab base height clears the wheel tops so nothing collides.

I'm tuning the track width and wheel thickness to avoid the wheels cutting into the body, settling on a track of 1.3 with 0.45 wide wheels so the body half-width of 1.05 (total 2.1m) keeps everything clear, while checking the container doesn't overhang too far past the wheels.

Now I'm working out vertical placement: the container sits from 1.45 to 3.0, the cab spans roughly 1.15 to 2.65, and I'm adding fender flares above the wheels to bridge the visual gap between wheel tops and the cab/container bottom. I'm also stacking up total height, factoring in a turret sitting on the cab roof.

I'm sketching helper functions for the build — box and cylinder creators, plus a neon glow helper that wraps parts with an emissive strength effect, making sure flat color strings are used instead of painted materials so the glow renders correctly.

Now I'm planning the texture set: hazard stripes for warning panels, a side emblem with "ARES-77 // NEON DIVISION" text and barcode styling, a cab door texture with a "07" marking and handle, vent grille lines, rear door details, and a cyan HUD screen texture for the turret.

I'm also working through the orientation math for placing these textured planes on the hull faces, figuring out how each plane's local axes map to world directions so the artwork reads correctly from the viewer's side.

For glow, I'll limit emissive texture coloring to screen panels only, keeping emblem panels non-glowing, and offset decal planes by 4mm to avoid z-fighting. Now I'm defining the core constants—track width, wheel radius/width, axle positions—and sketching the chassis as a dark box with rails, checking that axle spacing clears the wheel diameter.

Writing axle, differential, and driveshaft geometry, then designing a wheel function with a tire cylinder in near-black paint and tread lugs arranged radially around the circumference using rotated boxes.

Still refining wheel geometry...

Adding lug nuts and hub caps, then tallying parts per wheel at 22, totaling 132 across six wheels, before moving on to extruding the cab outline at z=1.0.

Writing cab extrusion settings...

Setting up a mottled gunmetal-teal panel paint with rivets for the hull, plus defining a separate accent paint layer.

Working out the cab roof profile points and windshield geometry, checking that the hood and windshield slopes line up correctly in dimension.

Now I'm placing hood details like the scoop box and vent plane slightly above the hood surface, noting that boxes in this setup show texture on all faces, and positioning the front grille plane facing outward near the hood's leading edge.

Still shaping the plow outline...

I'll texture the bumper box itself with the hazard pattern on all faces, then place the plow lower so it slightly overlaps without fully hiding it. For the cab, I'm adding door detail planes on the side faces using flat texture rectangles positioned at the appropriate height and depth.

Now I'm sketching side mirrors as thin rods extending from the cab with small mirror boxes at the ends, plus a roof-mounted light bar box.

Then I'm designing a turret for the cab roof: a rotating base ring, a boxy body, twin barrels extending forward with flash hiders, a side ammo box, and a sensor ball on top with a glowing red eye.

Now I'm building the cargo container structure: a main box frame with corner posts, top and bottom rails, and vertical ribs spaced every 0.7 units on both sides, plus emblem decals placed on the side panels.

I'm adjusting the rib and decal zones so they don't overlap — keeping ribs and cooling vents in the lower band while placing decals higher up, and adding a thin magenta neon glow strip along the lower edge. Then I'm adding rear double doors as a textured plane at the back face.

Now I'm working out the rear-facing orientation vectors to place details correctly, adding a rear bumper box and two red taillight boxes set just behind the bumper's back face.

Next I'm designing missile pods on the container roof: two tilted boxes with tube-circle textures on their angled front faces, rotated -30° about X so the fronts point upward, and computing the offset needed to position that textured face relative to each pod's center.

I'm also working out mounting geometry — a base box under each pod, checking whether the pod's rear corner clips into the container top, and adjusting the pod's vertical position so it sits just above the surface with some clearance.

I decide to reduce the pod's tilt angle and shrink its size slightly, repositioning it a bit lower to avoid an overly tall silhouette, then add small pivot support boxes on either side near the back. I'm sketching out a radar dish shape using a lathe profile, placing it on the front top of the container near the missile pods.

For the top details, I'm adding antenna rods with glowing tips at the cab's back corners, plus exhaust stacks positioned in the gap between the cab and container, complete with glowing orange caps and heat shield rings to fill that space neatly.

Now I'm placing side-mounted fuel/battery tanks between the front and mid axles, using horizontal cylinders with glow bands and strap details to fit cleanly in that open space.

I'm then adding wheel fender flares and mud flaps over the wheel wells, but checking that the front fender boxes don't clip into the wider cab body given their overlapping half-widths.

Now I'm placing underglow elements: thin cyan glow plates beneath the chassis and along the side edges so the glow is only really visible from below or at a low angle. Then I'm sketching cab steps, handrails, and roof-mounted details on the container -- vents, small crates, tie-downs, plus thin cyan neon trim strips running along the top edges.

Adding a kanji-style "ARES//2077" label, a side armor plate over the lower cab with chevron detailing, dual headlights with glow plus lower fog lamps, a tow hook and winch drum on the bumper, and faintly glowing windshield glass in a dark teal tone.

Working out the windshield as a tilted plane with dark glass and cyan HUD lines, computing its slope normal and offset so it sits correctly against the roofline...

Now I'm adding the side window texture, number plate, and a hatch ring on the cab roof, and roughly estimating total part counts across wheels, chassis, cab, container, turret, and pods to land somewhere in the 180-340 range. I'm also laying out the flat color palette for the dark trims—gunmetal, steel, tire black, cyan, magenta, orange, red, yellow, and more accent colors.

Now I'm designing the texture SVGs: an emblem panel with a pink stripe, hexagon logo, "ARES" wordmark, a cyan subtitle, barcode and warning details, and chevrons; plus a door texture with a cyan-gradient window, door number, handle, and magenta stripe.

Still writing SVG code...

Writing helper functions...

Still defining helper functions...

Adjusting lug radius to .66 so the sink stays within tolerance, then adding the hub, glowing cyan ring, cap, and six nuts arranged radially around the wheel. Now I'm moving on to writing the hull's panelled paint material.

Still working through the geometry details... placing vent textures on the lower side panels, a screen with a glow effect, and step boards near the front wheel axle. I'm mentally assembling all these container and cabin elements before composing the final structure.

Adding a handrail rod along the cab side, plus a sensor mast with a glowing tip and dipole whip, and roof-mounted antennas at the rear of the cab. Now ready to write everything out.
